title: Reconnection diagnostics for vortex tangles in Bose-condensed and superfluid dark matter halos
abstract: Bose-Einstein-condensed (BEC) and superfluid dark-matter (SFDM) halos can contain coherent, wave-supported cores whose angular momentum is carried by quantized vortices. When vortices form a tangle, reconnections convert part of the vortex kinetic energy into dark phonons, density waves, Kelvin waves, and vortex loops, providing a microscopic channel by which SFDM vortex structure can affect halo-core evolution. We estimate the dynamical importance of this channel by combining the local Gross-Pitaevskii reconnection law with a halo-scale vortex-line density calibrated against Schrödinger-Poisson simulations. In the minimal model the released energy stays in the dark sector, and standard-model luminosity requires additional portal physics.
summary: This paper analyzes how quantized vortex reconnections within superfluid dark matter halos can dissipate kinetic energy into various waves. By comparing the reconnection timescale to the halo's dynamical time using diagnostic ratios, the authors determine that this process is only dynamically important when the core is externally perturbed, not in relaxed equilibrium states.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamical and energetic importance of vortex reconnections occurring within Bose-Einstein-condensed (BEC) and superfluid dark matter (SFDM) halos.
main_result: Reconnection heating is only dynamically significant if the halo core is perturbed by mergers or tides, as relaxed cores show negligible energy release. The released energy remains in the dark sector, requiring additional physics for visible signals.
method: The authors combine a local reconnection law (derived from GPE theory) with a halo-scale vortex-line density calibrated against prior Schrödinger-Poisson simulations to calculate diagnostic ratios.
model_or_system: The system models dark matter halos as coherent bosonic media supporting quantized vortices, governed by principles related to the Gross-Pitaevskii equation. The dynamics are analyzed using concepts of vortex reconnection and energy dissipation into phonons/waves.
key_observables: Diagnostic parameters include $\chi = t_{	ext{dyn}}/t_{	ext{rec}}$, $t_{	ext{diss}}$ (dissipation time), and $\Pi_{	ext{rec}}$ (virial impact parameter).
important_parameters: Circulation quantum ($\kappa$), vortex-line density ($L$), dynamical time ($t_{	ext{dyn}}$), and core virial energy ($u_{	ext{vir}}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a local reconnection law and uses Mocz et al. (2017) results as an upper-bound proxy for the unknown vortex line density ($\eta_v$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical context of vortices in SFDM halos, derives local reconnection scaling laws, applies these laws to a halo-scale model using calibrated densities, and finally calculates diagnostic ratios ($\chi, t_{	ext{diss}}, \Pi_{	ext{rec}}$) to determine if reconnection heating is dynamically relevant.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from superfluid dynamics (vortex physics, GPE) with astrophysics (dark matter halos), providing a quantitative framework for energy dissipation in quantum many-body systems far from equilibrium.
